p.src: The Great Sage Sun admired the scenery of the immortal domain as he passed through the First, Second, and Third Gates of Heaven. When he reached the outer court of the Palace of Supreme Harmony, he suddenly saw five hundred divine officers clustered amid auspicious light and blessed vapors. One of the divine officers came forward to meet him and asked, “Who comes here?” The Great Sage replied, “I am Sun Wukong, the Great Sage Equaling Heaven. I wish to see the Revered Master.” Hearing this, the divine officers went in to report his arrival. The Patriarch immediately descended from his hall and welcomed him into the Palace of Supreme Harmony. The Pilgrim bowed and said, “I have a matter in which I must beg your help.” He asked, “What matter is that?” The Pilgrim said, “While escorting the Tang Monk to the Western Heaven to fetch the scriptures, we met with danger on the road. In the Western Continent of Cattle-Gift there is a mountain called the Little Western Heaven, and in its Little Thunderclap Monastery dwells a demon. When my master entered the monastery gate, he saw arhats, guardians, monks, and holy clerics arrayed before him. Taking them for true Buddhas, he had scarcely prostrated himself when the demon seized and bound him. I too was caught off guard. The demon cast a pair of golden cymbals over me, enclosing me without the slightest crack and clamping their rims together like pincers. Fortunately, the Golden-Headed Guardian reported the matter to the Jade Emperor, who dispatched the Twenty-Eight Lunar Mansions below that very night; but even they could not pry the cymbals open. Luckily, the Horned Wood Dragon thrust his horn inside and hauled me out. I smashed the golden cymbals, but the noise awakened the monster. As we pursued and fought him, he cast out a white cloth sack and swept me, the Twenty-Eight Lunar Mansions, and the guardians of the five directions into it, then bound us all with ropes. That night I escaped and rescued the star deities, the others, and my master, the Tang Monk. Later, while searching for our robes and alms bowl, we roused the monster again and fought him with the heavenly troops. The monster brought out the sack once more. When he began to work it, I remembered what had happened before and fled. All the others were swept into it again. Having no other recourse, I have come especially to beg the Revered Master for aid.” The Patriarch said, “In former years, when I exercised my might over the north, held the office of the Perfect Warrior, and eradicated demons and evil throughout the world, I acted under the Jade Emperor’s decree. Later, with hair unbound and feet bare, I trod upon the Soaring Serpent and Divine Tortoise and led the Five-Thunder divine generals, giant dragons and lions, fierce beasts and venomous dragons, to subdue the black vapors and demonic miasma of the northeast; that I did in obedience to a talismanic summons from the Celestial Worthy of Primordial Beginning. Now I dwell peacefully on Mount Wudang and repose at ease in the Hall of Supreme Harmony. For a long while the seas and mountains have been tranquil, and Heaven and Earth pure and prosperous. Since the demons of my Southern Continent and Northern Continent have been destroyed and the evil spirits have gone into hiding, I can hardly refuse to act now that the Great Sage has descended here. Yet without a decree from the upper realm, I dare not take up arms on my own authority. If I were to dispatch the gods without lawful authority, I fear the Jade Emperor would hold me guilty; but if I were to refuse the Great Sage outright, I would violate the obligations of friendship. I reckon that whatever demons may lurk on the western road cannot pose any very great danger. I shall therefore send the Tortoise and Serpent Generals and the Five Great Divine Dragons to assist you. They will surely capture the fiend and rescue your master from his peril.”

p.src: Meanwhile, the Great King Yellow Brows had gathered the fiends beneath the jeweled pavilion and was saying, “Sun the Pilgrim has not appeared these past two days. Who knows where he has gone to borrow troops?” Before he had finished speaking, a lesser fiend from the front gate came to report, “The Pilgrim has brought several dragons, a serpent, and a tortoise, and they are challenging us outside the gate.” The demon said, “How did that monkey come by dragons, a serpent, and a tortoise? From what quarter can such creatures have come?” He immediately donned his armor, strode out through the mountain gate, and shouted, “What company of dragon gods are you, that you dare invade my immortal domain?” The five dragons and two generals, imposing in appearance and full of vigor, cried, “You insolent monster! We are the five dragon gods and the Tortoise and Serpent Generals who serve the Demon-Subduing Heavenly Venerable, Primordial Patriarch of the Palace of Supreme Harmony on Mount Wudang. At the invitation of the Great Sage Equaling Heaven and by our Heavenly Venerable’s talismanic summons, we have come here to capture you. Fiend, quickly send out the Tang Monk and the star deities, and your life shall be spared; otherwise we shall hack every monster on this mountain to pieces and burn every room here to ashes.” Hearing this, the monster flew into a rage and said, “What powers have you beasts, that you dare make such boasts? Do not run! Taste my cudgel!” The five dragons churned clouds and summoned rain, while the two generals scattered earth and raised sand. Wielding spears, sabers, swords, and halberds, they all surged forward to attack; and the Great Sage Sun followed close behind, plying his iron staff. A fine battle it was:

p.src: The Pilgrim led the five dragons and two generals against the demon for half an hour, whereupon the fiend untied the sack and took it in his hand. Alarmed at the sight, the Pilgrim cried, “All of you, take care!” The dragon gods and the Serpent and Tortoise Generals did not know what they were to beware of. One after another, they checked their weapons and drew close to resist him. With a swish, the demon tossed the sack into the air. The Great Sage Sun had no time to concern himself with the five dragons and two generals. Mounting a somersault cloud, he leaped into the Ninth Heaven and escaped. The demon swept the dragon gods and the Tortoise and Serpent Generals into his sack once again. Victorious, the demon returned to the monastery, bound them with ropes as well, carried them into the cellar, and shut them in; of this we shall speak no more for now.

p.src: Look now at the Great Sage: he lowered his cloud and slumped on the mountaintop, utterly dispirited, lamenting, “That monster is terribly formidable.” Before he knew it, his eyes closed as though he were asleep. Suddenly he heard someone call, “Great Sage, do not pretend to sleep! Hurry and seek help at once. Your master’s life may end at any moment!” The Pilgrim opened his eyes, sprang up, and looked. It was the Duty God of the Day. The Pilgrim barked, “You petty god! Where have you been greedily feasting on blood offerings all this time instead of reporting for duty? And now you come to startle me! Stick out your shank and let Old Sun give you two blows to relieve his vexation.” The Duty God hurriedly bowed and said, “Great Sage, you are the joyous immortal of the mortal world. What vexation could you possibly have? We long ago received the Bodhisattva’s command to protect the Tang Monk in secret. Together with the local earth gods, we dare not leave his side even for a moment. That is why we have been unable to come and pay our respects regularly. Why, then, do you reproach us?” The Pilgrim said, “If you are his protectors, then where are the star deities, the guardians, the monastery gods, my master, and the others being held by the fiend? What torments are they suffering?” The Duty God replied, “Your master and junior disciples are hanging beneath the gallery of the jeweled hall, while the star deities and the others are suffering in the cellar. We had heard no news of you for the past two days. Just now we saw the demon capture the divine dragons and the Tortoise and Serpent Generals and send them into the cellar too. Only then did we realize that they were troops you had summoned, so this humble god came especially to find you. Great Sage, do not shrink from weariness. You must hurry once more to seek reinforcements!”

p.src: Hearing this, the Pilgrim could not help shedding tears before the Duty God. “Now I am ashamed to ascend to the Celestial Palace and abashed to visit the ocean treasury; I fear to ask the Bodhisattvas what to do, and dread appearing before the jade countenance of the Tathagata. Those just captured were the Tortoise, Serpent, Five Dragons, and other holy warriors of the True Martial Patriarch. I have no other way to seek aid. What am I to do?” The Duty God smiled. “Great Sage, take heart. I have recalled a company of elite warriors who, if invited, will surely subdue him. Wudang, which the Great Sage visited just now, lies in the Southern Jambu Continent. This force is also in the Southern Jambu Continent, at Pincheng on Mount Xuyi—the present-day Sizhou. There dwells the Great Sage State Preceptor King Bodhisattva, whose divine powers are immense. Under him is a disciple called Prince Little Zhang, together with four great divine generals; in former years they subdued the Lady of the Waters. Go and invite him in person. If he graciously comes to your aid, you will certainly capture the monster and rescue your master.” Delighted, the Pilgrim said, “Go and protect my master. Do not let them harm him while old Sun goes to seek help.”

p.src: The Pilgrim walked on as he looked about, until he came beneath the second gate. The State Preceptor King Bodhisattva had already learned of his arrival and came out with Prince Little Zhang to welcome him. After they had met and exchanged courtesies, the Pilgrim said, “I am escorting the Tang Monk to the Western Heaven to fetch the scriptures. On our road stands a Little Thunderclap Monastery, where a Yellow-Browed Monster impersonates the Buddha. My master could not distinguish true from false and bowed to him, whereupon he was captured. He also trapped me beneath a pair of golden cymbals, and only by fortune did a star spirit descend from Heaven and free me. I smashed the golden cymbals and fought him, but with a cloth bag he swept up the heavenly gods, the Guardians of the Five Quarters, the monastery guardians, my master, and my fellow disciples alike. I went to Mount Wudang to ask the Supreme Emperor of the Dark Heaven for aid. He sent the Five Dragons, Tortoise, and Serpent to seize the monster, but they too were swept into that bag. With no one left to rely upon, I have come to entreat you, Bodhisattva, to display your mighty power—the divine ability with which you subdued the Lady of the Waters and the wondrous means by which you save living beings—and accompany me to rescue my master from this calamity. Once we obtain the scriptures and return, they will be transmitted forever through China, proclaiming our Buddha’s wisdom and spreading the perfection of prajna.” The State Preceptor King replied, “Your present undertaking is indeed for the flourishing of our Buddhist faith, and by rights I should go myself. Unfortunately, it is early summer, precisely when the Huai River is in flood. I have only lately subdued the Great Sage Water Ape. That brute grows unruly whenever he encounters water, and I fear that if I leave, he will seize the opportunity to cause mischief, with no deity here able to restrain him. I shall therefore have my young disciple lead the four generals with you, to lend their strength in refining and subduing the demon.”

p.src: The young prince bore his white-paper-mulberry spear; still fiercer were the four Kunwu blades. Wukong wielded the golden-hooped staff, and all united to surround and slay the demon king. The demon king’s powers were truly great; wholly unafraid, he parried on every side. His wolf-tooth club was a treasure of the Buddha; neither sword cut nor spear stroke could harm it. Only the roaring of the furious wind could be heard, while malignant vapors spread in murky confusion. One side displayed its skills for mortal sport; the other devoted itself to worshipping Buddha and obtaining the scriptures. Again and again they charged; time after time they raged. They spewed clouds and mist that obscured the three lights; each fought in fury, anger filling every breast. Long had the supreme Dharma of the Three Vehicles been hindered, causing a hundred arts to struggle bitterly against one another.

One side displayed its skills for mortal sport; the other devoted itself to worshipping Buddha and obtaining the scriptures.
Again and again they charged; time after time they raged.
They spewed clouds and mist that obscured the three lights; each fought in fury, anger filling every breast.
Long had the supreme Dharma of the Three Vehicles been hindered, causing a hundred arts to struggle bitterly against one another.

p.src: All of them fought for a long while, but neither side prevailed. The fiend once more untied his bag. Again the Pilgrim cried, “Everyone, take care!” But the prince and the others did not understand what he meant by “take care.” With a sudden whoosh, the monster swept the four great generals and the prince alike into the bag. Only the Pilgrim, forewarned, escaped in time. Victorious, the demon king returned to the monastery. He had the captives bound with ropes and sent down into the cellar, which was firmly sealed and securely locked. Of this we shall speak no more for now.

p.src: The Pilgrim mounted his somersault cloud and rose into the air. Seeing the monster withdraw his troops and close the gates, he lowered his auspicious light and stood on the western hillside. Gazing sadly into the distance, he wept, “Master, I…”

p.src: Just as the Great Sage was sunk in misery, he suddenly saw a many-colored cloud descend in the southwest. A profusion of rain swept over the whole mountaintop, and someone called, “Wukong, do you recognize me?” The Pilgrim hurried forward to look, and there stood this person:

The Pilgrim hurried forward to look, and there stood this person:

p.src: At the sight of him, the Pilgrim hastily bowed. “Buddha Who Comes from the East, where are you going? Your disciple failed to stand aside and make way. A thousand pardons, a thousand pardons.” The Buddha said, “I have come expressly because of the monster at the Little Thunderclap Monastery.” The Pilgrim said, “I am deeply indebted to Your Reverence’s immense virtue and great kindness. May I ask what sort of creature that demon is, and from what place that fiend comes? And what manner of treasure is that bag of his? I beg Your Reverence to enlighten me.” The Buddha replied, “He is a Yellow-Browed acolyte who serves before me as keeper of the sounding stone. On the third day of the third month, I went to attend the Primordial Assembly and left him to guard the palace. He made off with several of my treasures, impersonated a Buddha, and turned himself into a fiend. That bag is my acquired bag, commonly called the ‘Human Seed Bag.’ And that wolf-tooth club is merely the mallet used to strike the sounding stone.” When the Pilgrim heard this, he cried aloud, “What a fine Laughing Monk you are! You let this acolyte escape, allowed him falsely to style himself the Buddha, and caused old Sun such misery. Surely you are guilty of failing to keep proper discipline in your own household.” Maitreya said, “For one thing, I was indeed careless and let a member of my household escape. For another, the demonic ordeals of you master and disciples were not yet complete. That is why so many spirits descended to the mortal world, and why you were destined to suffer this trial. Now I have come to help you take him back.”

p.src: The Pilgrim said, “This fiend possesses immense magical powers, and you have no weapon at all. How will you subdue him?” Maitreya smiled and said, “I have set up a thatched hut below this hillside and planted a field of melons and fruit here. Go challenge him to battle. When you fight, you must lose, not win, and lure him into my melon patch. All my other melons are unripe, but you are to transform yourself into one large ripe melon. When he comes, he will surely want a melon to eat, and I shall give you to him. Once you are inside his belly, you may deal with him there however you please. Then I shall take his pouch, put him inside it, and carry him back.” The Pilgrim said, “The plan is ingenious, but how will you recognize the ripe melon I have become? And how can we make him follow me here?” Maitreya smiled and said, “I am the World-Honored One who governs the age, and my wisdom-eye sees keenly. How could I fail to recognize you? Whatever form you assume, I shall know you. I fear only that the monster may refuse to follow you, so I shall teach you a spell.” The Pilgrim said, “He will certainly try to catch me in his pouch. Why would he follow me? What spell can bring him here?” Maitreya smiled and said, “Hold out your hand.” The Pilgrim at once opened his left hand and held it out. Maitreya dipped the index finger of his right hand in the divine moisture of his mouth and wrote the character “禁,” “restrain,” on the Pilgrim’s palm. He told him to clench his fist and then open it before the monster; the monster would follow him.

p.src: The Pilgrim clenched his fist and gladly accepted the instruction. Brandishing his iron staff in one hand, he went straight outside the mountain gate and shouted, “Demon! Your Grandpa Sun has come again. Come out quickly and let us see which of us is better!” A lesser demon hurried off again to report this. The demon king asked, “How many troops has he brought this time to challenge me?” The lesser demon said, “He has no troops at all. He is alone.” The demon king laughed. “That monkey has exhausted both his schemes and his strength and has nowhere left to seek help. He has surely come to offer up his life.” He promptly made himself ready again, took his treasure, raised his light and supple wolf-toothed club, and came out of the gate, crying, “Sun Wukong, you will not escape your plight this time!” The Pilgrim cursed him. “You wretched monster! Why should I not escape?” The demon king said, “I see that your schemes and strength are exhausted, that you have nowhere to seek help, and that you have come alone to make a desperate stand. Once I seize you now, no divine troops will come to rescue you. That is why I say you cannot escape.” The Pilgrim said, “This monster knows neither life nor death. Enough boasting! Take a blow from my staff!” Seeing him wield the staff with one hand, the demon king could not help laughing. “Look at this monkey trying to be clever! How can he fend me off while using his staff one-handed?” The Pilgrim said, “Son, you could not withstand me if I struck with both hands. If you did not use that pouch, even three or five more like you could not defeat Old Sun using just this one hand.” Hearing this, the demon king said, “Very well, very well! I shall not use my treasure now. I will fight you in earnest and see which of us is the better man.” He raised his wolf-toothed club and advanced to fight. Pilgrim Sun faced him, opened his fist, and wielded his staff with both hands. Struck by the restraining spell, the monster gave no thought to retreat. Sure enough, he did not use his pouch, but pursued the Pilgrim single-mindedly with his club. The Pilgrim made a feint, pretended defeat, and fled. The monster pursued him straight to the foot of the western hillside.

p.src: When the Pilgrim saw the melon patch, he somersaulted into it and immediately transformed himself into a large ripe melon, both sweet and fully ripened. The monster stopped and looked all around, not knowing where the Pilgrim had gone. He pursued as far as the hut and called, “Who planted these melons?” Maitreya had transformed himself into an old melon grower. Coming out of the thatched hut, he replied, “Great King, these melons were planted by this humble man.” The demon king asked, “Are there any ripe ones?” Maitreya replied, “There is a ripe one.” The demon king cried, “Pick me a ripe one to quench my thirst.” Maitreya immediately took the melon into which the Pilgrim had transformed and offered it to the demon king with both hands. The demon king suspected nothing. He took it in his hands and opened his mouth to bite. Seizing the opportunity, the Pilgrim rolled straight down his throat. Without waiting to see what might happen, he set hands and feet to work: clawing the intestines, raking the belly, turning somersaults, and standing on his head, tormenting the monster inside however he pleased. The monster grimaced in agony, tears filling his eyes, and rolled over the melon patch until it looked like a threshing floor. He could only cry, “I am finished! I am finished! Will no one save me?” Maitreya then revealed his true form and, chuckling merrily, called, “Evil beast, do you recognize me?” The monster looked up and saw him. In terror he fell to his knees, rubbing his belly with both hands and knocking his head against the ground as he cried, “Master, spare my life! Spare my life! I shall never do it again!” Maitreya stepped forward, seized him, removed his acquired pouch, and took away his mallet for striking the chime. He called, “Sun Wukong, for my sake, spare his life.”

p.src: The Pilgrim bitterly hated the monster, however, and struck with a fist on the left and a kick on the right, pounding and battering about wildly inside him. The monster, unable to endure the excruciating pain, collapsed to the ground. Maitreya said again, “Wukong, he has suffered enough. Spare him.” Only then did the Pilgrim call, “Open your mouth wide and let Old Sun come out!” Though the monster’s belly was racked with pain, he had not yet been mortally wounded. As the saying goes, “A man cannot die before his heart is harmed; when flowers wither and leaves fall, the root has dried.” Hearing the order to open his mouth, he bore the pain and opened it wide. The Pilgrim finally leaped out and resumed his true form. Just as he hastily drew his staff to strike again, the Buddha had already put the monster into the pouch and slung it across his waist. Holding the chime mallet in his hand, he cursed, “Evil beast! You stole my golden cymbals. Where have they gone?” The monster, intent only on saving his life, groaned and grumbled inside the acquired pouch, “Sun Wukong smashed the golden cymbals.” The Buddha said, “If the cymbals are broken, return my gold.” The monster said, “The broken gold is piled on the lotus pedestal in the hall.”

p.src: The Buddha, carrying the pouch and holding the chime mallet, chuckled and called, “Wukong, come with me to find my gold and return it to me.” Having witnessed such power, the Pilgrim dared not delay or disobey. He had no choice but to lead the Buddha up the mountain and back into the temple to gather the pieces of gold. They found the mountain gate tightly shut, but the Buddha pointed his mallet at it and the gate opened. When they entered, they saw that the lesser demons had learned their old king was captured. Each had gathered up his belongings and was preparing to scatter and flee for his life. Whenever the Pilgrim saw one, he struck one; whenever he saw two, he struck two. In this way he killed all five or seven hundred lesser demons. Each revealed its original form: mountain spirits and tree sprites, beastly fiends and bird demons. The Buddha gathered the gold into one place, breathed an immortal breath over it, and recited a spell. At once it returned to its original state, becoming a pair of golden cymbals once more. He took leave of the Pilgrim, mounted an auspicious cloud, and went straight back to the Land of Ultimate Bliss.

p.src: Only then did the Great Sage untie Tang Sanzang, Eight Rules, and Friar Sand. The idiot had been left hanging for several days and was wild with hunger. Without even thanking the Great Sage, he doubled over and ran straight to the kitchen in search of food. It turned out that the monster had been preparing his midday meal, but had not yet eaten it because Pilgrim had challenged him to battle. The idiot saw it and promptly devoured half the pot. Then he brought out two bowls and called his master and fellow disciples over, giving each of them two bowlfuls to eat. Only after that did he thank Pilgrim. When they asked how the monster had been subdued, Pilgrim recounted everything in detail: how he had first sought the Patriarch and the Tortoise and Snake Generals, then asked the Great Sage to lend him the prince, and finally how Maitreya had captured and subdued the fiend. When Tripitaka heard this, his gratitude knew no bounds. He bowed deeply to all the celestial beings and said, “Disciple, where are these holy ones being held?” Pilgrim replied, “Yesterday the Duty Officer of the Day told me that they were all in the cellar.” He called out, “Eight Rules, come with me and let us set them free.”

p.src: Strengthened by his meal, the idiot roused his spirits and found his rake. He then went with the Great Sage to the rear, opened the cellar, untied everyone’s ropes, and escorted them out from beneath the treasure tower. Tripitaka put on his cassock and bowed to each of them in thanks. The Great Sage then saw the Five Dragons and the two generals back to Wudang, Prince Little Zhang and his four generals back to Bincheng, and afterward the Twenty-Eight Lunar Mansions back to the celestial palaces; he also dismissed the Jiedi guardians and monastery protectors, each to return to his own domain.

p.src: The master and his disciples rested at ease for half a day. They fed the white horse its fill, packed their luggage, and set out early the next morning. Before leaving, they set a fire and burned all the jeweled towers, precious thrones, lofty pavilions, and preaching halls to ashes. And so it was that:
